title: Credit-based NCCL pipelining + KV-cache crediting and interleaved kernel launches
author: Aisha Patel
ci_summary: Unit + integration + bench smoke passed. Perf-suite flagged two marginal regressions on synthetic long-seq TP jobs; rerun with warm-cache shows stable or improved 95th p99 latency for our canary models.
release_notes: Introduces credit-based NCCL pipelining and a KV-cache crediting mechanism to reduce host-side stalls and improve overlap between communication and compute for multi-GPU tensor-parallel workloads. Backwards compatible; rollout behind env flag `REDWOOD_TP_CREDIT_PIPELINE`.
description:
Motivation: multi-GPU tensor-parallel workloads were seeing intermittent host stalls when KV cache prefetches and NCCL collectives contended for host resources. Existing scheduling overlapped collectives and compute but lacked a lightweight flow-control primitive to prevent head-of-line stalls and excessive kernel serialization. This PR introduces a credit-based pipelining layer for NCCL collectives and ties credits to KV-cache prefetch hooks so that expensive prefetches yield to in-flight collectives while preserving throughput.

Summary of changes: 1) credit_allocator: a new lock-free credit pool per TP group that tracks outstanding collective windows and grants up to N credits to launch interleaved kernels; 2) nccl_launcher: modified to consume/return credits and to attach a small metadata token to hostbuffers (hostbuf credit id) so host-side RPCs and prefetches can yield; 3) kv_cache_prefetch: integrates with the allocator to request and optionally defer prefetch work if credits are low; 4) kernel_interleaver: lightweight scheduler in the runtime that issues smaller micro-kernel launches (sub-chunked GEMM/softmax) when credits permit to improve overlap; 5) autotune: adds a conservative heuristics path that picks initial credit counts per model shape and per-cluster bandwidth tier; 6) metrics and tracing: new metrics tp.credit_grants, tp.credit_waits, tp.prefetch_yields and tracing tags to correlate stalls with credit starvation.

Benchmarks: ran canary suite on 8xA100 (NVLink) and 4xA40 (ethernet). Representative results vs main (median of 10 runs): - 8xA100 TP transformer-20b throughput +12% and 95th token latency -17% under mixed short/long sequences; - 4xA40 TP 7b pipeline saw 9% throughput improvement and p99 latency -14% for batched streaming workloads; - tail-case with pathological large KV prefetch previously causing 400ms host stalls now drops to <50ms and is handled by backpressure. Microbenchmarks show average NCCL host-buffer contention window reduced by ~65%.

Compatibility and rollout: change is behind feature flag REDWOOD_TP_CREDIT_PIPELINE and controlled by per-deployment config. Default disabled for older Dedicated clusters until a canary roll completes. No model format change. Autotune values are conservative to avoid regressions; customers can set explicit credit counts in route configs.

Testing: unit tests for allocator (race-free invariants), integration tests exercising interleaved launches with mocked NCCL, end-to-end perf canary on perf-canary infra, chaos test where KV prefetch threads are artificially delayed (passes). Added a regression test that injects credit starvation and asserts graceful defer of prefetch rather than host OOM.

Files changed (high level): runtime/tp/credit_allocator.cpp, runtime/tp/nccl_launcher.cpp, runtime/tp/kernel_interleaver.h, runtime/tp/kernel_interleaver.cpp, runtime/kv/kv_prefetcher.cpp, runtime/kv/kv_prefetcher.h, runtime/metrics/tp_metrics.cc, tools/autotune/tp_credit_tuner.py, tests/unit/test_credit_allocator.cpp, tests/integration/test_interleaving_e2e.py, docs/operations/credit_pipeline.md, examples/tuning/credit_examples.yaml, and minor changes to the canary deployment manifest and CI bench harness.

Implementation notes and rationale: credits are intentionally lightweight (16-bit counters) to avoid memory pressure and to be easy to serialize in hostbuf metadata. We chose an optimistic consume-return model instead of a token-queue to reduce host lock contention; fast-path avoids atomic ops for single-GPU launches. The interleaved micro-kernel launches split larger matmuls into contiguous sub-chunks aligned to cache lines to avoid additional memory traffic. The KV prefetcher now exposes a `try_prefetch_with_credit` API that either performs the prefetch or returns a suggested backoff window which runtime uses to schedule a deferred task.

Rollout plan: merge to main gated by perf canary and staged canary rollout to 10% of hosted clusters then to Dedicated alpha clusters. Feature flag default off for existing Dedicated customers until telemetry confirms stable tail latency.

Documentation: added ops doc with knobs and troubleshooting, and tuning examples for 4/8/16 GPU clusters explaining credit counts and expected behavior.

Known limitations: current autotune is conservative and may underutilize high-bandwidth topologies; future work will introduce dynamic credit adaptation based on live telemetry. Edge cases: on extreme heterogenous mixes the allocator may starve small collectives; mitigations include a prioritized credit queue (planned follow-up).

Checklist: - [x] unit tests - [x] integration tests - [x] perf canary runs - [x] docs updated - [x] feature flag added

Related: builds on ideas from ENG-987 experimental interleaver and references SUP-4421 customer incident where KV prefetches caused repeated host stalls.

review_comments: Jonah Kim: Nice approach. Two asks: (1) can we expose a debug endpoint to snapshot credit state per-GPU for debugging, and (2) please document the heuristics used in autotune.
Aisha Patel: Added /_debug/tp/credits and expanded docs section with autotune heuristics (see docs/operations/credit_pipeline.md).
Miguel Santos: Observability additions look good. On the allocator: please ensure we don't introduce ABA by reusing small credit ids — prefer epoched ids or 32-bit tag.
Aisha Patel: Switched hostbuf token to 32-bit composed of credit_id:epoch to avoid ABA; updated tests accordingly.
Priya Rao: CI perf flakes earlier on ethernet cluster; after rerun numbers look acceptable. Approving pending a changelog entry.
Aisha Patel: Added changelog entry and release_notes; running a final perf canary on 4xA40.
merge_commit_message: Credit-based NCCL pipelining + KV prefetch crediting: reduce host stalls and improve TP overlap. (ENG-1289)
notes_for_ops: Feature gate REDWOOD_TP_CREDIT_PIPELINE. Default is OFF for Dedicated until canary window completes. Debug endpoints: /_debug/tp/credits and /_debug/tp/credit_metrics. If customers see regressions, disable feature and gather tp.credit_waits and tp.prefetch_yields metrics for triage.
